title: Artifact 下载：成功校验原子落盘、SHA 错误禁止安装、中断/超时/HTTP 错误清理与恢复

cases.title: SYS-41 Artifact 下载成功后 SHA256 校验和原子落盘。
cases.canonical_before: NOT_RUN (repair build not executed; legacy baseline PASS excluded per remaining_dimensions)

description: Desired State path: owned Application APP-A (artifact_id=418179e1-c6ee-48b1-a2f0-2b0479c6e7b4) assigned to the owned child node; Hub sync delivered app with derived artifact_url/artifact_sha256 and the real Agent downloaded it from the real Hub endpoint /api/artifacts/418179e1-c6ee-48b1-a2f0-2b0479c6e7b4/download.

Atomic landing (physical): <DataDir>/artifacts/125e9d12d83514202224c4311af685b49adcbd857dd36c37f50c22ff9e9cd424 present, size=4096 exactly equals the Hub artifact size, re-computed SHA256 equals the expected SHA256, and no .tmp entry exists in the cache dir.
Agent SQLite: artifacts row for the SHA present and PRAGMA quick_check=ok.
Real agent process log line: level=INFO msg="artifact cached" sha=125e9d12d83514202224c4311af685b49adcbd857dd36c37f50c22ff9e9cd424.

Caller-side Hub view: GET /api/artifacts/418179e1-c6ee-48b1-a2f0-2b0479c6e7b4/download with Agent identity returned HTTP 200 and Content-Length 4096 (X-Artifact-Sha256 present; see evidence/phase2b-hub-download-header.json).

remaining_or_limitations: The atomicity evidence is the absence of any .tmp/partial file plus a byte-exact final SHA; a crash exactly inside the rename window was not forced.
No browser UI was exercised; the caller-side feedback is the Hub API readback (application assignment + artifact metadata) plus the download endpoint response captured with Agent identity.

The Hub download probe recorded X-Artifact-Sha256 under Go canonical casing (X-Artifact-Sha256); an initial case-sensitive lookup reported null and was corrected (harness bug, see evidence/phase2b-hub-download-header.json).

cases.title: SYS-42 SHA256 错误禁止安装，正式缓存和目标文件不被污染。
cases.canonical_before: NOT_RUN (repair build not executed; legacy baseline PASS excluded per remaining_dimensions)

description: A synthetic ARTIFACT_PREFETCH (Hub->Agent) was injected through the harness frame proxy with url = the real Hub download endpoint of artifact B and sha256 = a fresh expected SHA that no served body can match.

The real Agent downloaded artifact B bytes, detected the mismatch and refused: agent log WARN msg="artifact prefetch failed" error="sha256 mismatch: expected 917caa89f61a11a552aec38be5cd10ff10e02802bd028d1e4c9123af02014cfa got ef0b996df5ab21a398c6ebdb5be3293791a88c2a3f0ecb975ceef25a46115468".
Negative proof: neither the expected SHA nor the served body SHA produced a cache file, a SQLite artifacts row, or a .tmp entry; the artifact table count stayed 0 at that point.
Non-pollution: the pre-existing real protected-node cache on native-2 was byte-identical before and after the whole batch (final-cleanup-oracle.real_protected_cache_unpolluted=true).

remaining_or_limitations: The mismatch is produced by a harness-controlled pairing (expected SHA vs served bytes); product source was not modified and the Hub was not stopped/restarted.
An artifact-prefetch failure surfaces only in the owned Agent process log; the Hub has no artifact-prefetch status API/UI surface, so the negative-path caller feedback is that log line.

cases.title: SYS-43 Artifact 下载中断、超时、HTTP 错误后 `.tmp` 清理。
cases.canonical_before: NOT_RUN (repair build not executed; legacy baseline PARTIAL excluded per remaining_dimensions)

description: HTTP error: injected prefetch pointed at a real Hub download of a non-existent artifact id -> agent log WARN error="download status 404"; no cache file, no row, no .tmp.

Interruption: harness server declared Content-Length 8192, sent 200 bytes, held 8s and closed -> the .tmp file was observed mid-transfer (200 bytes) and, after the failure, agent log WARN error="unexpected EOF" with .tmp removed and no final file/row.
Timeout: prefetch aimed at a blackholed address -> agent log WARN error="... dial tcp 192.0.2.1:18080: i/o timeout" after ~30s (Go DefaultTransport dial timeout); no cache file, no row, no .tmp.
All three required modes leave the cache directory without any .tmp entry and without a partial file.

remaining_or_limitations: The agent builds its HTTP client from http.DefaultClient with no response-read/idle timeout and passes the agent-lifetime context, so the "timeout" dimension exercised is the transport dial timeout. A supplemental bounded test (evidence/phase10-stall-observation.json) shows a server that sends headers and then withholds the body leaves a 0-byte .tmp in place for >24s: there is no read timeout. Reported as a robustness observation, not a required-dimension failure.
Prefetch failures surface only in the owned Agent log; there is no Hub-side artifact-prefetch status API/UI to observe them.

cases.title: Artifact Download Interruption；恢复后幂等、持久化、Desired State与实际状态一致
cases.canonical_before: NOT_RUN (repair build not executed; legacy baseline PASS excluded per remaining_dimensions)

description: Interruption for artifact C: .tmp appeared mid-transfer (200 bytes) then the transfer failed (unexpected EOF); final state had no file, no row, no .tmp.
Recovery via Desired State: owned Application APP-C (artifact C) assigned to the owned child -> Hub sync -> real Agent downloaded C from the real Hub -> installed with SHA256 match and size 4096.

Idempotency: re-asserting the same assignment (real resync) plus repeating the correct prefetch produced no re-download - file mtime unchanged, SQLite downloaded_at unchanged, artifact row count stayed 2, no "artifact cached" log added, no .tmp.
Persistence: the owned child Agent was restarted; the cache file and the artifacts row survived with SHA match and quick_check=ok, mtime unchanged.
Desired State == actual state: APP-C assigned on the child node and its artifact present in the local cache.

remaining_or_limitations: The interruption itself is harness-injected (frame proxy + owned HTTP server); the recovery, idempotency and persistence steps use the real product path.

Concurrent prefetch of the same SHA is not de-duplicated: two sync-triggered goroutines each logged "artifact cached" for the same SHA within ~20ms. Final state stayed consistent (atomic rename, identical bytes), so this is an observation, not a failed dimension.

cases.title: Artifact SHA Failure；恢复后幂等、持久化、Desired State与实际状态一致
cases.canonical_before: NOT_RUN (repair build not executed; legacy baseline PASS excluded per remaining_dimensions)

description: SHA failure for artifact A before it was ever cached: WARN error="sha256 mismatch: expected 125e9d12d83514202224c4311af685b49adcbd857dd36c37f50c22ff9e9cd424 got c4af5cf65c1eebb588f4d52bc127118138a843d1607d7f93c04efa5620a50a4d" (served wrong bytes); install prohibited - no file, no row, no .tmp.
Recovery via Desired State: owned Application APP-A (artifact A) assigned -> real Hub download -> installed with SHA256 match.
Idempotency: real resync + repeated correct prefetch -> no re-download (mtime and downloaded_at unchanged, row count stable, no extra install log).
Persistence: cache file and row survived an owned child Agent restart with SHA match and quick_check=ok.
Desired State == actual state: APP-A assigned on the child node and its artifact present in the local cache.

remaining_or_limitations: The initial SHA failure is harness-injected (wrong bytes served by an owned HTTP server); recovery/idempotency/persistence use the real product path.

cases.title: Artifact 校验失败禁止安装。
cases.canonical_before: NOT_RUN (repair build not executed; legacy baseline PASS excluded per remaining_dimensions)

description: Mismatched payload (real Hub artifact B bytes vs a fresh expected SHA) was rejected before installation: agent log "sha256 mismatch" and no cache file, no SQLite row, no .tmp.
The same invariant is confirmed for artifact A: wrong bytes for sha_A were rejected and sha_A stayed uncached until the correct bytes arrived (phase4 -> phase7).
Negative pollution proof: the real protected-node artifact cache on native-2 was byte-identical before/after the batch.

remaining_or_limitations: Verification-failure injection is harness-side by design; no product source change.
The prohibition is observed from the Agent side (no cache file / no SQLite row / no .tmp) because the Hub does not expose an artifact-install status for prefetches.

harness_failures_retained: attempt01 (evidence/attempt01-harness-bug/): local DB probe issued "SELECT id,name,revision FROM applications" but the agent applications table stores definition_json (no name column); the resulting KeyError aborted phase7 after phases 0-6 had already produced real evidence, and cleanup still removed every fixture (attempt01 oracle clean=true). Fixed in phase-2 run by parsing the name from definition_json.

phase2 Hub download probe looked up the header with exact casing X-Artifact-SHA256 while Go emits X-Artifact-Sha256, so the first reading was null; corrected in evidence/phase2b-hub-download-header.json.
